title: 5 Rules for Better Error States
summary: This reel provides five actionable tips to improve UX by properly handling error states. It covers matching error types to UI patterns, providing recovery paths, and using live validation to prevent errors before they occur.

transcript.text: Your error states are killing users. Five fixes.
Type the error first. Validation, network, server, permission. Each one needs a different visual pattern.
Don't show a 500 modal for a typo.
Every error needs a way out. Retry, refresh, contact us. A dead end is the worst experience you can ship.
Severity decides the surface. Inline for recoverable, toast for transient, modal only when nothing else works.
Replace "An error occurred" with "Lost connection, reconnecting in 5 seconds". Humans read humans, not machines.
Inline validation kills 80% of errors before they happen. Disable submit until valid, show progress, catch problems early.
Prevent. Don't catch. Save this for your next error state. Follow for more UI systems.

on_screen_text: RECOVERY: Every error needs an exit.
COPY: Words do most of the work.
PREVENTION: Inline validation kills 80% of errors.
design_principles: Match the error type to the surface
Always offer a way out (recovery actions)
before_after: A generic 'Error 500' modal with an 'OK' button is transformed into a contextual 'Lost connection' toast with 'Try again' and 'Refresh' options.
